newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch-Belgian Fortis nine-month profit up 18 pct.
newsitem.headline: Dutch-Belgian Fortis nine-month profit up 18 pct.

text.p: Dutch-Belgian financial group Fortis on Thursday announced an 18 percent increase in net profit to 554 million ecus ($697 million) for the first nine months of 1996.

The unlisted banking and insurance group, jointly owned by Fortis Amev of the Netherlands and Fortis AG of Belgium, also said it expected net profit for the full year to be between 12 and 15 percent higher than a year earlier.
Analysts had expected a nine-month net profit of about 549 million ecus from the group, formed through the 1989 merger of the Dutch and Belgian companies.
The listed parent companies also unveiled higher earnings with the Fortis results and said they saw their full-year profits at least 10 percent higher than a year ago.
Fortis Amev annnounced a 17 percent rise in net profit to 605 million guilders for the same period, while Fortis AG's nine month net profit rose 21 percent to 10.05 billion Belgian francs.

After the results, Fortis Amev shares were at 56.00 guilders at 1110 GMT, up 90 cents from the previous close, while Fortis AG shares were at 4870 francs, up 30 francs. ($ = 0.794 European Currency Unit ECUs)
